_comment: The A4 threshold decision as taken for Tier 2, frozen. preregistration_tier2.md sec 1 requires Tier 3 to
differ from Tier 2 in exactly one variable, the size and composition of the source pool, with the same
metrics and the same protocol. The regime boundary formula is part of that protocol, so it is decided
once and applied to every species thereafter rather than re-selected as the candidate table grows.
This file exists because on 15-09-2026 profiling eleven Tier 3 bird candidates re-ran the A4 tree over the
whole accumulated table and moved the universal rule from 0.1 x p50 to 0.00603816 x p90. boundary_m() reads
selected_boundary_m live from results/regime_profiles.csv, which is gitignored, so that silently changed the
strata underneath a sealed evaluation: Larus fuscus 411.45 -> 181.88 m, Canis lupus 131.30 -> 46.32 m,
Mirounga angustirostris 1609.44 -> 213.17 m. Tracked here so the decision cannot move again unnoticed.
Reproduce with: regime_profile.py --decide-threshold --reselect, which is the only path that re-selects.
tier2_boundaries_m added 16-09-2026 (A16 follow-up): A16 froze the rule but not the numbers, and boundary_m()
still read selected_boundary_m from the gitignored CSV, so re-profiling a role species could move a boundary
under the same rule. These are the six values every stored Tier 2 output was computed with; the three
held-out values equal regime_boundary_m in results/tier2_sealed/tier2_verdict.json. boundary_m() now returns
these for role species and fails if the CSV disagrees. Stork is 61.10 m here; the 60.9 m in A1/A4 is
reference_boundary_m, the calibration constant for the p75/p90 branches, and is unused under 0.1 x p50.
registered_under: preregistration_tier2.md A4, scope fixed by A16
reasons: all species passed the median-anchor guards
